questions.q: For the scenario in this lesson — notify a group's manager when a new Priority 1 Incident comes in — which trigger type is correct, and why?
options: A Scheduled trigger, because notifications should go out on a fixed daily schedule
A Record trigger, because the automation is reacting to a new Incident being created, not running on a timer
Either trigger type works equally well for this scenario
No trigger is needed since Notify actions run automatically on their own
questions.explain: This is a reaction to something happening — a new Incident arriving — which per Lesson 3 calls for a Record trigger, not a Scheduled trigger.

questions.q: In Step 1, why is the trigger's change type set to "Created" rather than "Updated"?
options: Because the request is about catching the Incident the moment it's new, not reacting to later edits
Because "Updated" triggers are not supported in Flow Designer
Because "Created" always fires faster than "Updated"
It doesn't matter which one is chosen for this scenario
questions.explain: The business request is about a new Incident coming in, which maps to Created — Updated would instead fire on every later edit to the record.

questions.q: Why does the trigger also need the condition "Priority is 1 - Critical"?
options: Without it, the flow would fire on every new Incident regardless of priority, which isn't what was requested
Conditions are required on every Record trigger even when not needed
The condition changes which table the trigger watches
The condition determines whether the flow is a Flow or a Subflow
questions.explain: The condition is what narrows the trigger down to only the Incidents that actually matter for this request — Priority 1 - Critical ones.

questions.q: How does the Notify action in this scenario determine who receives the notification?
options: It always sends to a single hardcoded recipient typed once into the action
It uses a data pill referencing the triggering Incident's Assignment Group, resolving to that group's manager dynamically for each Incident
It sends to every user on the instance
It requires a separate Scheduled trigger to determine the recipient
questions.explain: The recipient is resolved dynamically through a data pill off the triggering record's Assignment Group, not a fixed value typed once.

questions.q: What is the real difference between saving a flow and activating it?
options: There is no difference; saving and activating are the same action
Saving deletes the flow, while activating creates it
Saving preserves the configuration without running it against real records; activating is the deliberate step that turns the trigger engine on
Activating is required before you can even add a trigger
questions.explain: A newly built flow is inactive by default. Saving preserves your work; activating is the separate, deliberate step that makes the trigger start watching for matching records.
